correctness.rationale: Functional calculus at x≥0 reduces the normalized error to [L(z)−a tanh(z)]/4 with z=h(lambda+x)/4 and a=w−1. Differentiation gives sech²(z)(J(z)−a). Re-expanding the stated hyperbolic quotient in z² cancels the constant and linear terms and gives positive denominator coefficients b_n and numerator ratios 4^n/[(2n)(2n−1)]−1 for n≥2. The ratios strictly increase, so cross-multiplying the series derivative and pairing indices gives strictly positive terms (m−n)b_m b_n(r_m−r_n) for m>n. Thus J increases from 1/3 to infinity. For 1/3<a<1, the error falls from 0 to one negative minimum then rises to 1−a; the height of the negative minimum is continuous and strictly increasing in a, and crosses 1−a exactly once. To prove the global minimax immediately, every Re(a)<a_* worsens the limit at infinity and every Re(a)>a_* worsens the finite negative contact, regardless of imaginary part. At Re(a)=a_* a nonzero imaginary part already worsens the modulus at infinity. These contacts are available in essential supremum on the multiplication model whenever h*lambda/4≤z_*, including equality by continuity in x. For all other spectra only the universal upper bound is asserted. At w=4/3 the real error is increasing to 2/3 in scalar units, giving exactly h/6 on the unbounded model. Independent Decimal bisection reproduces the displayed z_*, w_*, C_* and improvement ratio (python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence/reproduce.py, output 4); the uploaded diagnostic was read but not executed. The analytic proof, not finite sampling, covers the whole half-line.

value.rationale: Smooth-vector cancellation and full-spectrum operator error are competing objectives for a natural, already used two-grid rule. The sharp universal constant and uniqueness quantify that distinction: the optimum improves the classical unbounded-spectrum error constant by a factor about 2.61 without promising a higher rate. The fixed continuous-spectrum model explains which scales force the optimum. The guarantee does not address finite time truncation, sampling noise or general nonnormal semigroups.
